notes.title: Update for this month
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

I’ve been working feverishly behind the scenes to get everything ready for the first major update, which I’m hoping to release before the end of Q1—possibly even the first week of March. There’s been a huge amount of work going into the game, adding new content, fixing issues, and making improvements. I’ve kept my head down focusing on this, and I’m excited to share what’s coming soon!

In the coming days, I’ll be posting a detailed patch notes list covering everything included in the Q1 update. There’s a lot to unpack, so keep an eye out for that. I’ll also be sharing a roadmap outlining the updates planned for the rest of the year, so you know what to expect.

On top of the development work, I’ve also been applying for funding through Scottish EDGE and a few other funding bodies. If successful, this would help speed up development and allow me to expand the game even further. The goal is to bring you more content, better systems, and fully voice-acted, high-quality quests—because let’s be honest, boring fetch quests just aren’t my style. I want every quest to feel like a quality experience, with a bit of that signature brutal humor you’ve come to expect.

Being a solo developer means things can take a bit longer, but I’m fully committed to delivering a complete game that lives up to your expectations. Your patience and support mean the world to me.

We recently had a successful playtesting session at the GamesHUB Playpazook event. The feedback was invaluable. It highlighted a few areas needing improvement, including rebuilding the mini-map system and making quest objectives and goals clearer. I’m already working on these changes to ensure the final product is as polished as possible.

There’s so much happening, not just with the game but also with growing Haggis Goes Wild Studios into something bigger than I ever imagined. Bigfoot vs Scots is shaping up to be something truly special, and I can’t wait to see where we go from here.

Thanks for being part of this journey!

notes.title: Happy Hogmanay and Huge thanks for your support
notes.content:
[h1]Happy Hogmanay and Best Wishes for 2025![/h1]

As we usher in the New Year, I want to extend my heartfelt gratitude to everyone who supported Bigfoot vs Scots by purchasing the game. Your enthusiasm means the world to me, and I truly hope you enjoy playing it as much as I’ve enjoyed creating it.

[h2]Reflecting on 2024[/h2]
This past year has been a challenging yet rewarding journey. Releasing Bigfoot vs Scots into Early Access marked a significant milestone for me as a solo developer. Amidst the whirlwind of moving countries three times, I’ve finally settled in Scotland, and it feels incredible to call Dundee home. Haggis Goes Wild Studios has firmly planted its roots here, and I feel incredibly fortunate to be part of Dundee’s vibrant and supportive game development community.

Dundee’s legacy as the birthplace of iconic games like Lemmings, Grand Theft Auto, APB, and Pine Hearts is a testament to the city’s talent and innovation. The positivity and camaraderie in this industry hub have been unlike anything I’ve experienced. Over the past six months, attending conferences, talks, and meetings has been instrumental in my growth as a developer—a title that still feels surreal, even after five years of hard work.

[h2]Post-Launch Updates and Progress[/h2]
Following the launch of Bigfoot vs Scots, I took a much-needed break to rest and reflect. This downtime allowed me to evaluate my processes and refine my approach for future updates. Since then, I’ve returned to development with renewed focus.

Recently, I spent a productive day at CoStar Labs at Abertay University recording motion capture for the game. This experience was invaluable, saving me weeks—if not months—of animation work. I’m excited to incorporate these polished animations into the game in upcoming updates.

Another major focus has been the development of The Wee Rab storyline and questline. After weeks of writing, coding, testing, and asset creation, it’s nearly complete and starting to take shape. I look forward to sharing it with players in the New Year.

[h2]The 2025 New Year Patch[/h2]
Initially, I planned to release a Christmas update, but I decided to consolidate the content into a single, comprehensive New Year Patch. This update will include new questlines, additional content, and fixes for bugs identified at launch, ensuring a richer experience for players. Expect this patch to drop in early January.

[h2]Looking Ahead to 2025[/h2]
Creating new content and questlines is one of the most rewarding aspects of development, but it’s also a time-intensive process—especially as a solo developer. This year, I hope to bring in additional help, offering opportunities for newcomers in the industry to gain valuable experience. While resources are limited at this time, I’m optimistic about growing the team and continuing to expand Bigfoot vs Scots with frequent updates and engaging new content.

In the coming weeks, I’ll share an updated roadmap for 2025, outlining plans for future updates and milestones. I’m excited to keep building on what we’ve achieved and to deliver more memorable experiences for players.

Thank you again for your support and encouragement throughout this journey. I hope you had a wonderful holiday season and wish you an incredible 2025.

Warm regards,
Haggis Goes Wild Studios

notes.title: After Early Access: The Future of Bigfoot vs Scots
notes.content:
[h1]After Early Access: The Future of Bigfoot vs Scots[/h1]

First, let me take a moment to thank everyone who has supported Bigfoot vs Scots up to this point. The Early Access launch is a monumental milestone for me and Haggis Goes Wild Studios, and I couldn’t have done it without the amazing players who’ve laughed, cursed, and explored the absurd yet lovable world I’ve created. Your feedback, support, and enthusiasm have shaped this game in ways I never imagined, and for that, I am deeply grateful. But Early Access isn’t the end of the journey—it’s just the beginning. So, let’s talk about where Bigfoot vs Scots is headed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805818/37786ba8d8d2f21f0ae8af518e6fd9d932add14c.jpg[/img]

[h2]Expanding the Cast: New Characters on the Horizon[/h2]
One of the biggest and most exciting additions coming post-launch is the introduction of new characters that will bring fresh humor, challenges, and chaos to the island. Here’s a sneak peek:

[list]
[*] [b]Bean-nighe[/b] :The harbinger of doom, this supernatural washerwoman has a habit of scrubbing blood-stained clothes by the riverbank, foretelling death. In Bigfoot vs Scots, she might just take a break from predicting doom to nag you about laundry etiquette or offer some surprisingly sage advice—if you can decipher her thick Highland accent.

[*] [b]Am Fear Liath Mòr [/b](The Big Grey Man) :Towering and mysterious, this folklore-inspired giant brings a mix of terror and hilarity to the Highlands. Don’t let his imposing presence fool you; he has a soft spot for poetry and a surprisingly fragile ego.

[*] [b]A Bogle[/b] :Mischievous, spectral, and slightly unhinged, the Bogle thrives on chaos. Whether it’s setting bizarre traps or engaging in nonsensical riddles, you’ll need your wits (and a lot of patience) to deal with this trickster.

[*] [b]The Loch Ness Monster[/b] :Of course, no game set in Scotland would be complete without Nessie. Expect an unconventional take on the famous cryptid—she’s less about hiding in the loch and more about taking the piss out of tourists and locals alike.
 
[*] [b]Stagenwolf[/b]: A wolf-like creature with deer-like horns that roams the forest, adding yet another mysterious element to the island.
[/list]

These are just some of the creatures that will be getting added in the next patch in March.

[h2]More Quests, More Shenanigans[/h2]

With these new characters come new questline's that stay true to the comedy and absurdity that defines Bigfoot vs Scots. These quests will explore new areas of the island, dive deeper into Scottish lore, and push the boundaries of just how ridiculous—and heartfelt—a game like this can be.
From helping Bean-nighe sort out her “laundry list of grievances” to untangling a centuries-old feud between Nessie and a clan of Angry Neds (NED = Non-Educated Delinquents), every new storyline will bring fresh laughs and unexpected twists.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805818/6907cee014ca438e73f6273d1d259d52d2b883c2.jpg[/img]

[h2]Listening and Growing[/h2]

Early Access is an opportunity for me to connect with you—the players—and ensure that Bigfoot vs Scots delivers on its promise of comedy and absurd adventures. That connection doesn’t stop with the launch. Your feedback has been, and will continue to be, at the heart of this project.
Expect more patches, updates, and refinements as I polish the existing content, balance gameplay, and implement community suggestions. Whether it’s adjusting Hamish’s epic sporran quest or fine-tuning the menu system, every tweak is a step toward making the game the best it can be.

[h2]The Timeline for What’s Coming[/h2]

While this is not carved into a Pictish stone, I hope this will give you an idea of where I plan to go forward with things.

[h3]After Early Access Launch[/h3]

The first part will focus on bug fixing and sorting out any core gameplay issues. As a solo developer, please be patient with me—it might take a little time to get to the bottom of each problem, but they will be fixed. I will update you on when those fixes are coming, hopefully with small hotfixes rolling out quickly.

[h3]The Hogmanay Update[/h3]

I plan to drop some special New Year's Day content for those who have bought the game before the end of the year. It will include some holiday-themed shenanigans and a couple of extra questlines to keep you busy.

[h3]The March Update[/h3]

The big March update will feature an extensive amount of new quests and characters to interact with. Now that the main game mechanics are mostly in place, I can focus on fleshing out the island, adding more things to do and explore, and hopefully many more laughs along the way. This will also mark the introduction of a couple of new planned features:

[list]
[*] Pickup and power-ups
[*] Mob drops
[*] Weapon pickups and power-ups
[*] Skill tree system and XP system
[/list]

[h3]The Summer Update[/h3]

The next big update after that will be the Summer Update, which will focus on adding more to the questlines, content, locations, and hopefully some of the planned features, including:

[list]
[*] Armor, rings, and special item equipment system
[*] Clothing and item swapping
[*] Possibly a mount system
[/list]

There will be more to come after that, but I’ll review things after each patch to see where the best direction for the game is, based on player feedback. I want you to be at the core of this game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805818/6f8b98104369c2bfcfc5636accd53dc9ea3f8bc4.jpg[/img]

[h2]Looking Ahead[/h2]

While the road after Early Access is long, I’m committed to seeing it through. There’s so much more to explore, and the possibilities for Bigfoot vs Scots are as vast as the Scottish Highlands themselves. My dream is to grow Haggis Goes Wild Studios from a solo developer into a small, dedicated team that can keep expanding this world while creating new, equally outrageous games in the future.
For now, I’ll continue to pour my heart and soul into Bigfoot vs Scots, knowing that the best is yet to come. Thank you for believing in this weird, wild adventure. Together, we’ll keep the madness going.

Slàinte,
and a big thanks from me

I am very pleased with the outcome and the efficiency gains this exercise provided.

So though I would share,

notes.title: A Cheeky Update
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

It’s been about a month since my last update, and let me tell you, it’s been a wild ride. Over the past six months, I’ve had to move three times, and it’s been a whirlwind of chaos—honestly, a proper cluster mess. But the good news is, I’ve finally found some stability. My visa situation has been a rollercoaster—first declined, then won on appeal, only to have that overturned. But, I’m back home in Scotland now, and I can finally breathe easy without worrying about visa issues.

Behind the scenes, I’ve been quietly plugging away on the game and the Early Access (EA) trailer. So, let’s dive into the juicy details you’re here for—the game!

After sharing a pre-release demo with a few folks, I received some fantastic feedback, and I’ve really taken it to heart. The consensus was that there needed to be more things to do. While I’ve already fleshed out a fair number of questlines, it was clear I needed to add more content to the EA build. Of course, the final game will have hundreds of quests, but for EA, I’ve been hard at work adding a few new characters and finishing up their questlines.

I also received feedback on some bugs, spelling and grammar issues, and a few voice lines that needed polishing. I’m happy to say that all the questlines in the EA build are now fully voiced. I’ve also done some camera tweaks to smooth out the gameplay experience and fix those annoying glitches.
Now, let me introduce you to a couple of new faces on the island:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805818/8888feb092454666009d8798a43657b090a847eb.jpg[/img]
Hamish MacBeardieFace: A Highlander who got lost on his way to work and somehow ended up on the island. There’s a whole new questline around helping Hamish find his way—or maybe he’ll just settle in!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805818/aa18fdd5dcbaa55eefb10066b953dd1553e41e1b.jpg[/img]
Wee Rab: The local NED (Non-Educated Delinquent) who’s always up to no good. He’ll have you running around the island trying to locate his elusive stash. Be prepared for a bit of mischief!

Both characters are fully modeled, rigged, and in the game, with their questlines nearly finished. I’m also working on recording their voice lines and making a few final tweaks.

Beyond that, I’ve been busy tweaking the landscape, refining foliage, reducing loading times, and fixing up the menu system, which got a bit buggy in the last build. There’s still so much more to come, and I’m really excited about the upcoming Early Access release.

I apologize for the delay, but now that I’m settled with a proper office, stable internet, and a place to work, things are moving forward steadily. Expect more updates in the coming weeks, along with a couple of “making-of” videos I’ve got in the pipeline. So keep your eyes peeled, and don’t forget to upvote the post if you’re excited about what’s to come!

Thanks for sticking with me on this journey—there’s a lot more ahead!

Cheers!

notes.title: Weekly Developer Update
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

Another week has passed, and it's been a busy one for me. I've been hard at work, tweaking and fixing various aspects of the game.

Here's what I've been up to:

New Quests: I created 5 new quests this week featuring Robbie, Mrs. McG, and Kenny the Haggis. I won't go into too much detail, but spending a few hours figuring out what werewolf poo looks like was quite an interesting experience.

Dialogue System: I’ve refined the dialogue system to align with the game's theme and style. Getting it to work in the build version was challenging, but I managed it. Now, the quest system and dialogue system interact seamlessly, making quests more fun and engaging for players.

Loading Screen: The loading screen is now fully operational and themed to match the rest of the game.

Graphics: I've overhauled the Steam page, adding new screenshots and text to give a more current idea of what the game is about. There are a few more tweaks to come.

Trailer: I’ve been working on the game trailer, filming the combat systems, and tweaking the enemies. We currently have at least 16 unique enemies, and I plan to add more in the coming months.

What's coming up?

The next few weeks are going to be very busy:

Steamfest: Bigfoot vs Scots is taking part in the next Steamfest. I'll be launching a demo that will be playable for a week.

Live Stream: I’ll be streaming the first preview of the game on June 12th at 8 PM UTC. During the stream, I'll announce the Early Access release date.

I'm excited to share all of this with you and look forward to getting the demo ready to submit to Steam in time. Exciting times ahead!

Thanks for following along!

notes.title: Developer Update Week 21
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

I’ve been hard at work preparing our game for submission to Steam for Early Access. Yes, Early Access is almost here!

A wee sneak peak at the trailer, still lots to be done, but some combat, more on that later. 

[previewyoutube=hrcMG1nBiZ0;full][/previewyoutube]

I’ve been focusing on creating a stable build of the game, fixing various bugs, including the issue with the start screen widget not showing in the build version. I also spent an afternoon optimizing textures, reducing draw calls, and implementing mipmaps for texture streaming. This ensures that textures are lower resolution at a distance while maintaining detail up close—a pretty satisfying task!

In addition, I have a couple of essays coming your way about the use of AI and what it means to me. Stay tuned for those.

Combat System Updates
I've been polishing the combat system, making it more fluid and intuitive. It’s starting to feel much better, though there are still a few tweaks needed. Overall, I’m pleased with the progress.

What's Coming Next Week?
The trailer, which I hope you've seen, is my main focus right now. There’s a lot going into it, including scenes with Mrs. McGreggor, movie-like sequences, and in-game cutscenes. I’m working on ways to clearly indicate what’s cinematic and what’s actual gameplay footage.

The next big task is the Quest and Dialogue system. They’re functioning well, but adding more quests is a top priority. The quest lines for Early Access are nearly complete, but adding voice acting in the given timeframe is challenging. Initially, some quests will be text-based, allowing me to spend time recording voice lines and setting up cutscenes. These will be included in one of the first updates.

So, quest lines are the next big thing. There’s a lot done but still plenty to go. I’ll be working on that while also dedicating time to the trailer and some gameplay videos. Hope this keeps you up to date on what I’m doing.

Thanks for your support!

Cheers,

notes.title: A Weekly Update Week 20
notes.content:
Hello everyone

I just returned from my exciting, adventurous four-day drive across Europe. It was an epic journey that provided ample time to contemplate the Bigfoot vs. Scots game and our future plans.

Let's discuss the coming week. Understandably, there hasn't been much progress on the game due to my travels and the unpacking that followed. However, I did make some headway on the swimming system. Currently, it supports swimming on the water's surface, with plans to introduce underwater diving in the future.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805818/5c97ad5862439180953ee665ee05a9b6b72adb9c.jpg[/img]

Here's what's coming up this week:

Roadmap: I aim to finalize a roadmap for the upcoming year, outlining plans for major updates, as well as space for smaller updates, patches, and hotfixes.

Gameplay Footage: I plan to release actual gameplay footage featuring some of the characters.

Short Talks: I'm working on 1-2 minute videos where I discuss the game and its production. My goal is to eventually combine these short talks with gameplay footage, behind-the-scenes content, concept art, and early designs.

Polish Combat System: I'm finalizing the combat system, which I'm quite pleased with. However, I still believe the key layout needs improvement, though players will have the option to customize their keys. I also hope to have controller support ready for the Early Access launch.

By the end of the week, I aim to announce a release date for Early Access, which I hope will be in the next couple of weeks.

The Discord server is now up and running with a permanent link added. I will be active on the server to answer any questions or receive feedback. I look forward to engaging with you.

Here are some additional tasks I'm focusing on:

Completing quest lines (some need models and dialogue finished)
Polishing dialogue for certain quest lines
Adding a Tam o' Shanter to the Werehaggis (model is made, needs rigging)
Setting up loading screen tips (loading screen is functional, tips need to be added)
Ensuring all houses have doors
Finishing ladder animations
Fixing the save and load game feature (now fixed)
Adding weapon pictures to the UI
Thank you for your patience and support. I'm excited about the progress we're making and can't wait to share more updates with you soon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805818/89ba2bb508c74c7d8750ff29fdb8299b977d4aa8.png[/img]

notes.title: A Weekly Update Week 18
notes.content:
Hey all, dropping in for another weekly update. This week has been a bit chaotic for me as I'm gearing up to move house next Tuesday. I'll be hitting the road for about four days, making my way to a new country. It's exciting stuff, but it's also meant that I haven't been able to dedicate as much time to the game as I would have liked. Next week is shaping up to be a bit of a clusterf***, but once I'm settled, I'll have a solid three weeks to really dive into the game. My belongings won't arrive for another three weeks, so it'll just be me, my computer, my gaming chair, and plenty of time to focus.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805818/97c182308a76a99f85f36e10735f48a1834b0ed5.png[/img]

Now, onto the important stuff—what I've been working on. I've managed to get the Quest system, Combat System, and Dialogue system all talking to each other and sharing information, which is a big win. Check out the Options menu in the screenshot—I've got some basic settings that can be adjusted. Next up, I'll be tackling key bindings, and I'm hoping to have that sorted by next week, even if I'm sitting in a tent at a campsite somewhere in Europe!

I've also been putting some work into the music system, and I'll be posting a more detailed update about that over the weekend. Additionally, I'm in the process of putting together an 'Early Access Road Map', outlining my plans and timelines. Stay tuned for that.

On the web front, I've finally got the website up and running at BigfootvsScots.com. I'll be posting plenty of information there, but rest assured, major updates will always be shared here as well.

It's mostly been a lot of housekeeping tasks lately—cleaning up things in the blueprints, tweaking here and there. I'm also hoping to share some game footage soon, but I can't commit to specific dates just yet. Once I'm settled in my new home, I'll be able to provide more consistent updates. As any creative will tell you, a little chaos is necessary to create something special.

Until the next update, stay safe, stay healthy, and enjoy life. And as a bonus, here's a little treat for you: drunk haggis dancing on the Rusty Badgers bar. (NSFW)

https://youtube.com/shorts/fV6KTRzVi10

notes.title: first of the weekly updates and news on Early Access
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805818/d0b59f1df28c6896655232745c2f0da0a47d7ab0.jpg[/img]
[h1]Early Access[/h1]

I guess first I should announce the that Early Access is going to be coming in May, The date has not been set, but I am hoping everything will be ready for around the middle of May, and will have date announcement a few weeks before that. 

[h1]Weekly updates[/h1]

My plan is have weekly updates on here on what's been going on with game and what has been done, with photos and the odd video. So here first of my updates and look forward hearing from you all. 

The most recent work that has been done has been toward getting the start screen, loading, and saving systems working. For the moment, it will be set up to 10 slot options, with plans for an expansion to name and select as many saves as you want in the future. Additionally, I've been working on a combat system, getting AI to attack, move, and strafe around the player, while also being aware of each other. I've also set up attacking sounds and getting hit noises. Recently, I imported custom weapons textures and set them up so I can assign them to any AI using game tags. I've also been creating custom animations for some of the monsters, like the werewolves, and set them up to have both bipedal and quadrupedal versions of the enemy. I hope to add dogs and wolves next, and hopefully, that will be done by the end of the week.

I'm also working on dialogue and quests now. I've finalized a lot of dialogue trees in Twine and am working on integrating those dialogue trees into the game's dialogue system and linking them up with quests.

Next week's plan is to continue working on that and get the majority of the main quest lines for Part One of the story finished, with players meeting up with most of the main characters and such. Music is going to be an important part of that too, but I will talk more about that next week.

notes.title: The Holiday and Early Access Update and New Trailer
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805818/0302bf819e4b571c888e3017d8e4d75b966f22a7.png[/img]

[previewyoutube=kN_PQa41a-o;full][/previewyoutube]

[u][b]Greetings, dear gaming enthusiasts![/b][/u]

It's been a wild ride in the fantastical world of our game, where Mrs. McGregor and her quirky companions, the wee beasties, have been burning the midnight oil to inch closer to the coveted early access stage. We're thrilled to spill the beans that we're gearing up for an early access launch in the next couple of months. Hold on to your kilts, because we've got a lot on our plate, but we're convinced we're on the brink of unveiling something truly worth your gaming hours.

Let's break it down for you in a way that even Bigfoot could understand:

[b]Game Systems[/b]:

Quest System: Almost there, just needs a bit of polishing—like giving a Highland cow a good brushing.
Dialogue System: Almost ready to shine, just needs a few tweaks to make the characters' banter as delightful as a Scottish sunset.
Combat System: Basics are in place, but there's still some heavy lifting ahead—think of it as lifting bagpipes.
Act One Storyline: Done and dusted! We've crafted a tale more gripping than a Loch Ness monster sighting.
Voice Overs: Almost there, just a few touch-ups and reworkings to ensure you hear Mrs. McG's wisdom loud and clear.
Quest Lines: Written and planned—like looking for werewolf poo-filled adventures.
Foliage and Grass System, River and Water System: We're landscaping experts now, with separate post-processing to make the environment as picturesque as a rolling Highland meadow.

[b]Characters that are ready to rumble[/b]:

Mrs. McG (of course),
Ann,
Bigfoot Early,
Bigfoot Hammer,
Robbie the Barman,
Cpt Lack.

[b]Areas that are polished and ready for your virtual footsteps[/b]:

The Black Kirk,
Bigfoot Camp,
The Castle,
Rusty Badger,
Scottish Flemish Houses and Harbour Area,
Village One and Village Two,
The Murder House,
The Rectory,
The Church of Bigfoot,
Mrs. McGregor's Front Room.

Now, let's talk about our grand plans for the game's future:

[b]Game Scope Redefined[/b]:

As time has marched on, and we've gotten closer to our early access release, we've had to put on our big-boy kilts and make some tough decisions. Some features we originally planned just need more time than a bagpipe solo at a ceilidh or simply didn't quite fit the story we're weaving.

[b]Features Out ([/b]for now, at least):

Multiplayer (Might make a grand entrance later, like a mythical creature in the mist).
Co-op (Could join the party fashionably late).
Pre-game Character Customization (Sorry, but we're sticking to the storyline script).
Companion System (It's complete and functional, but it's like trying to fit a caber into a kilt—it just doesn't work with our theme).

[b]Coming Soon After Early Access[/b]:

Loot drops with different weapons (because who doesn't love an upgrade?).
Clothing drops and Character Customization (Time to give your character a makeover).
Multi Skill Trees (Get ready for some serious character growth).
Companion Haggis (Yes, you read that right—ride on your shoulder and conquer the Highlands together).
We're aiming to deliver a gaming experience that's more thrilling than a Highland fling and more satisfying than a plate of haggis, tatties and neaps. As we approach the finish line of our almost 4-year journey, we want to assure you that we're not promising the moon but a gaming experience that'll leave you smiling.

Have a fantastic holiday, share the game with your mates, and any thoughts or feedback you have will be cherished more than a bottle of fine Scotch. Cheers to you, our fellow adventurers!

notes.title: A Little Update
notes.content:
Hey there, Bigfoot vs Scots community!

We wanted to share a quick update on the development progress of our beloved game. As always, we're working hard to bring you the most immersive experience possible, and that commitment currently has us deep in the development trenches of our combat system and character design.

Our team is diligently crafting the intricacies of the combat system, aiming to make every encounter as thrilling as it is strategic. We're weaving in the unique strengths and skills of both Bigfoot and our Scottish warriors, ensuring each battle is distinctive and keeps you on your toes.

Parallel to this, we're also fully engaged in the character design phase. We're pouring our creativity into each character, from our burly Bigfoot to the gritty Scots, to bring you unforgettable personalities that are as vivid as the landscapes they inhabit.

While we're itching to reveal more, we want to ensure everything is perfect before pulling back the curtain. Therefore, we ask for your patience. We're just as excited as you are, and we promise the wait will be worth it.

We genuinely appreciate your support and enthusiasm for Bigfoot vs Scots. Your passion is our driving force, and we can't wait to share what we've been brewing. Stay tuned for more updates in the near future!

Keep the excitement alive!

Team Bigfoot vs Scots
